sources.title: Rüdiger Schmitt, Aryans: linguistic definition (Encyclopaedia Iranica)
sources.note: Used only for the linguistic definition and relationships of Vedic, Indo-Aryan and Iranian. This 1987 article contains dated migration reconstructions; those are not adopted. Indexed original read.

sources.title: Michael Witzel, Early Sanskritization: Origins and Development of the Kuru State (1995)
sources.note: Primary philological argument. Indexed original PDF pages 4, 9, 11 and 23 read; direct PDF requests failed. Historical model attributed, not equated with an archaeological ethnic map. Whole work budget combines all uses.

sources.title: UNESCO, Tradition of Vedic chanting
sources.note: Indexed original at https://ich.unesco.org/en/lists?RL=00062 read; canonical page direct request challenged. Use only four collections, living oral pedagogy and continuity. Do not repeat erroneous statement that Vedic derives from Classical Sanskrit, speculative zero claim or undated current branch counts.

sources.title: Rig Veda, R. T. H. Griffith translation: selected hymns
sources.note: Directly checked hymn pages rv01001.htm (1.1.1), rv09112.htm (9.112.3), rv10034.htm (10.34.2 to 5, 13) and rv10085.htm (10.85.26 to 27, 36, 42, 46). All pages charged as one work. Poetry is evidence of expressed concerns and ideals, not a demographic survey.

sources.title: GRETIL, Rigveda Mandala 1, Aufrecht edition in Roman transcription
sources.note: Header identifies Aufrecht second edition 1877, digitized by Van Nooten and Holland; accents omitted. Direct line RV_1,001.01a: agnim īḷe purohitaṃ. Translation is a concise rendering checked against Griffith 1.1.1. Modern Roman transcription, no contemporary manuscript claimed.

sources.title: Maurice Bloomfield, Hymns of the Atharva-Veda (1897)
sources.note: Direct full edition: 4.12 fracture charm; 3.30 family concord; 11.5.3 to 6 disciple initiation and firewood. Ancient religious statements, not clinical evidence or advice. All selections one budget.

sources.title: K. N. Dikshit, Excavations at Hulas (1978 to 1983), ASI Memoir 113 (2020)
sources.note: Downloaded public report to cache and read extracted text. Printed pp. 7 to 8 regional PGW and Hulas Period II; pp. 158 onward Period II small finds; chapter 7 pp. 195 to 197 chronology. Late Harappan remains are earlier contextual evidence, not identified as Vedic speakers. No toilet claim made.

sources.title: Chandogya Upanishad 6.13, Max Müller translation (1879)
sources.note: Direct text of salt-water teaching dialogue, printed pp. 104 to 105. Literary philosophical example, not claimed as a documented classroom experiment.

sources.title: Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 3.8, Max Müller translation (1884)
sources.note: Direct and indexed original checked, printed pp. 136 to 139: Gargi challenges Yajnavalkya with two questions. A particular literary portrayal of learned debate, not universal female educational access.

proposedOverrides.name: Vedic Indo-Aryan communities
proposedOverrides.summary: Diverse Vedic textual communities and Indo-Aryan languages, not a single empire.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Separate culture card; no aliases associated.
batchIdentityNotes.map: Indexed circa -1500 to -500. Three imported features have broad bounds documented in identities.json. Public overview distinguishes language, text, archaeological culture and political boundaries.
batchIdentityNotes.chronology: Phase divisions are approximate editorial teaching intervals, not sharply dated transitions or a migration calendar. Neither the modern national borders nor a fixed pan-Indian empire is inferred.
batchIdentityNotes.evidence: Textual prescriptions and literary voices are not universal household statistics. Hulas supplies comparative archaeological evidence without linguistic or ethnic attribution. No toilets or sanitation system claimed from this evidence. Sanskrit is modern Roman transcription of orally transmitted text.
